verdict.rationale: Expensify's own docs show SmartScan reading receipt merchant, date, total and currency, and auto-categorizing expenses from policies and past behavior. Automatic receipt-to-card matching avoids duplicate entries. A hands-on community report says categorization is wrong about 70% of the time unless the expense is obvious, which weakens the categorization claim. Missing for 10: memo suggestions, fraud or anomaly detection, explicit duplicate detection beyond receipt-to-card matching, and reliable independent corroboration of categorization accuracy.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, AI codes and audits expenses for me — reading receipts, suggesting categories and memos, and catching duplicates or fraud

citations.quote: SmartScan reads the merchant, date, total, and currency automatically.
Expensify uses your policies and past behavior to auto-categorize expenses as they're created.
The scanned receipt matches to the card transaction automatically, with no manual matching or duplicate entries.
